subject.title: Anthropic setup-token onboarding path has multiple failure modes (docs gap, credential propagation, multi-agent sync)

question: Should Anthropic setup-token/manual-token credentials be physically copied to sibling agent stores, inherited through main-store read-through, or handled only with validation and clearer setup guidance?
rationale: This choice affects sensitive credential propagation across per-agent stores and must stay consistent with the current policy that OAuth refresh material is not portable by default.

options.title: Narrow static-token availability
options.body: Make Anthropic token credentials available to sibling agents through an explicit static-token-only sync or inheritance path while keeping OAuth refresh material non-portable.

options.title: Read-through plus validation only
options.body: Keep the current read-through model, add post-write validation and clearer setup-token guidance, and avoid new physical credential copies.

options.title: Defer to bulk auth tooling
options.body: Keep this issue open but route cross-agent sync semantics to the broader bulk rotation/sync design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47684.

recommendation.title: Narrow static-token availability
recommendation.body: Make Anthropic token credentials available to sibling agents through an explicit static-token-only sync or inheritance path while keeping OAuth refresh material non-portable.

likelyOwner.reason: The read-through auth-store fix and current credential-sharing boundary route most directly through this owner history.
